note.subject: french
note.title: Future time
note.overview: This lesson contains 50 enabled questions. It teaches Future time through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Future time.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Core production target: futur proche = aller in the present + infinitive.
Only aller is conjugated; the action verb stays infinitive.
Use a future time phrase to make the frame clear.
Negatives wrap around aller: je ne vais pas + infinitive.
Simple-future items in this section are recognition/light exposure.

questionInstructions.label: APPLY THE RULE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Produce the exact item requested by the rule prompt.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted English and write the complete French answer.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO ENGLISH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted French and write the complete English meaning.

questionInstructions.label: COMPLETE THE FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Do not translate the whole line; write only the word/chunk replacing _____.

questionInstructions.label: CHOOSE THE ANSWER
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Select exactly one option.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the taught French example meaning « I am going to watch a film. ».
workedExamples.why: Pattern: je vais + infinitive. The example places every grammar word in its taught position.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the taught French example meaning « You are going to play tennis. ».
workedExamples.why: Pattern: tu vas + infinitive. The example places every grammar word in its taught position.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the taught French example meaning « She is going to buy a pizza. ».
workedExamples.why: Pattern: il / elle va + infinitive. The example places every grammar word in its taught position.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the taught French example meaning « We are going to go out in town. ».
workedExamples.why: Pattern: nous allons + infinitive. The example places every grammar word in its taught position.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the taught French example meaning « You are going to finish your homework. ».
workedExamples.why: Pattern: vous allez + infinitive. The example places every grammar word in its taught position.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the taught French example meaning « They are going to drink orange juice. ».
workedExamples.answer: Ils vont boire du jus d’orange.
workedExamples.why: Pattern: ils / elles vont + infinitive. The example places every grammar word in its taught position.

commonMistakes: Conjugating both verbs.
Using a future phrase with a completed-past verb.
Treating extension simple future as the core target.

nous _____ sortir en ville
Write only the correct form of aller.
“You are going to finish your homework.”

vous _____ finir vos devoirs
Write only the correct form of aller.
“They are going to drink orange juice.”

ils _____ boire du jus d’orange
Write only the correct form of aller.

mustMemoriseRules: Imperfect gives background or repeated past habits.
Useful chunks: j’étais, j’avais, c’était, il y avait.

note.title: Daily routine toolkit
note.overview: This lesson contains 51 enabled questions. It teaches Daily routine toolkit through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Daily routine toolkit.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Build routine sentences with time + action + detail.
Mix reflexive and non-reflexive verbs.
Use d’habitude for present habit, hier for completed past, demain for futur proche.
In reflexive perfect forms, check pronoun, être and agreement.
Finish with an opinion or reason.

note.subject: french
note.title: School descriptions
note.overview: This lesson contains 79 enabled questions. It teaches School descriptions through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for School descriptions.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: École is feminine; adjective forms must match.
Learn facilities with articles.
After il n’y a pas/il n’y avait pas, use de/d’.
Present school: est/il y a; primary school past: était/il y avait.
Lesson times use commencent/finissent à.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Comme clubs, il y a / il y avait…
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: As for clubs, there is / there was…

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: un club de danse / de musique / de sciences / de théâtre / de gymnastique
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: a dance / music / science / drama / gymnastics club

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: un club de foot / de netball
un gymnase / un terrain de sport / une cour
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: a gym / a sports field / a playground

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: un CDI / une bibliothèque / une cantine / un internat
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: an LRC / library / canteen / boarding house

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: des salles de classe / des laboratoires
il n’y a pas de / il n’y avait pas de…
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: there is not / there was not any…

note.subject: french
note.title: School activities
note.overview: This lesson contains 50 enabled questions. It teaches School activities through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for School activities.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: On means we but takes il/elle grammar.
Present uses one finite verb; perfect uses auxiliary + participle.
avoir→eu, faire→fait, lire→lu, apprendre→appris, écrire→écrit.
Use time clues to select present or past.
Rewrite the whole phrase when changing tense.

questionInstructions.label: CHANGE THE TENSE

workedExamples.why: Source pair: on a trop de devoirs → on a eu trop de devoirs (we have / had too much homework). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: on a des discussions intéressantes
workedExamples.answer: on a eu des discussions intéressantes
workedExamples.why: Source pair: on a des discussions intéressantes → on a eu des discussions intéressantes (we have / had interesting discussions). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: on travaille dur
workedExamples.why: Source pair: on travaille dur → on a travaillé dur (we work / worked hard). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: on fait des expériences
workedExamples.why: Source pair: on fait des expériences → on a fait des expériences (we do / did experiments). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: on s’amuse
workedExamples.why: Source pair: on s’amuse → on s’est amusé (we have / had fun). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: on lit des poèmes / des romans
workedExamples.answer: on a lu des poèmes / des romans
workedExamples.why: Source pair: on lit des poèmes / des romans → on a lu des poèmes / des romans (we read / read poems or novels). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

commonMistakes: Writing on travaillons.
Using an infinitive after on a.
Missing the past participle.

note.title: Reflexives and negatives
note.overview: This lesson contains 62 enabled questions. It teaches Reflexives and negatives through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Reflexives and negatives.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Reflexive perfect: pronoun + être + participle.
Feminine/plural agreement is required where shown.
Body-part phrases such as brossé les dents normally keep brossé.
In perfect negatives, put pas/jamais/rien/plus around the auxiliary.
Keep the reflexive pronoun inside the negative frame.

questionInstructions.label: CHANGE THE TENSE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Rewrite the entire French phrase in the named tense.

questionInstructions.label: CONJUGATE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Use the named subject/tense. The bare verb or correct subject + verb is accepted when stated.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted English and write the complete French answer.

questionInstructions.label: COMPLETE THE FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Do not translate the whole line; write only the word/chunk replacing _____.

workedExamples.why: Source pair: je me lève → je me suis levé(e). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: je me lave
workedExamples.why: Source pair: je me lave → je me suis lavé(e). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: je me comporte bien / mal
workedExamples.answer: je me suis bien / mal comporté(e)
workedExamples.why: Source pair: je me comporte bien / mal → je me suis bien / mal comporté(e). Keep the auxiliary and past participle together.

workedExamples.prompt: Change this taught form to the perfect tense: je m’ennuie

note.title: High-scoring structures
note.overview: This lesson contains 52 enabled questions. It teaches High-scoring structures through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for High-scoring structures.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Choose connectives by purpose: sequence, contrast, time, reaction or comment.
ce qui est/était comments on the preceding idea.
après avoir + participle links two actions by the same person.
A connective must join complete, meaningful ideas.
Do not list linkers without using them accurately in writing.

note.title: Targeted practice
note.overview: This lesson contains 58 enabled questions. It teaches Targeted practice through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Targeted practice.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Dictation requires exact base spelling and grammar chunks.
Translate complete sentences, not isolated words.
For perfect negatives, check auxiliary and word order.
For reflexives, check pronoun, être and agreement.
After correction, record the error type and retest after 48–72 hours.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Mon école est un collège de filles à Kingston qui s’appelle Tiffin.
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: My school is a girls’ middle school in Kingston which is called Tiffin.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Il y a une chorale et un orchestre, mais il n’y a pas d’internat.
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: There is a choir and an orchestra, but there is not a boarding house.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Mon école primaire était plus petite et plus tranquille.
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: My primary school was smaller and quieter.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Ma matière préférée, c’est l’histoire parce que c’est passionnant.
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: My favourite subject is history because it is exciting.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Je suis forte en musique, mais je ne comprends rien en français.

note.title: Classroom objects
note.overview: This lesson contains 89 enabled questions. It teaches Classroom objects through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Classroom objects.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Learn every classroom noun with un/une and its plural.
After a number above one, use a plural noun.
Plural articles use des.
Spelling of the noun still matters when the article is correct.
Dans mon sac, il y a… is the core sentence frame.
